2.text: For the female the system is practically the same, except that in the

3.text: table of affinity the takaˊlhɪn (“wife’s sister’s husband”) relation is not found.

4.text: THE FAMILY GROUP. — A group of kindred families is designated by

5.text: the term vaˊrat (literally, “collection of those who are together”). Va is the

6.text: root of the verb vaˊrkin (“thou art”), -ret, -rat, signifies “collection” (see p. 539).

7.text: A member of the same family-group is called ᴇnaˊn-varaˊtkên (“one of the

8.text: same vaˊrat”). In modern times, however, this term has acquired a broader

9.text: meaning, and is used in the sense of “people,” “folk;” though for the latter

10.text: idea there exists another word, reˊmkɪn (“people,” “folk”). Still another term

11.text: for the family-group is more characteristic. It is čiˊn-yɪrɪn (“collection of those

12.text: who take part in blood-revenge”). Čin is the stem of the word liˊñliñ (“heart”¹),

13.text: but is used also for blood-revenge. Liˊñɪlɪn means “blood-avenger.” This

14.text: term čiˊn-yɪrɪn is used frequently, because the vendetta still exists in full vigor.

15.text: The Chukchee vaˊrat may perhaps be called an embryo of a clan; it is,

16.text: unstable, however, and the number of families that “are together” changes

17.text: almost every year. Moreover, when one vaˊrat picks a quarrel with another

18.text: one (usually one living in the neighborhood), there will always be a few families

19.text: that are connected equally with both interested parties. The centre of the

20.text: vaˊrat forms a group of brothers, and secondarily a group of cousins, both

21.text: of which are called “a group of boys.” A proverb says, “The group of boys

22.text: is disposed to scoff” (Kraˊtɪčhɪn nɪkoˊraqên). This means that numerous

23.text: brothers who keep together may abuse any of their neighbors with impunity.

24.text: On the other hand, the lonesome one (kuwliˊkɪlɪn) is always downcast. He

25.text: speaks humbly, he lives in poverty, and is subjected to the abuse of families

27.text: In cases of blood-revenge, brothers and cousins are the first to come

28.text: forward. For instance, in the year 1895, among the Chukchee of the Big

29.text: Anui River, two young men of different families disputed over the dividing

30.text: of a mammoth-tusk which they had found in the tundra. In the ensuing

31.text: quarrel one of them picked up his rifle and shot at the other, though without

32.text: success. A quarrel among the families ensued. The man shot at belonged
